hook: Fake trading app takes *₹2.3 crore* from RC Puram retiree
hook_b: Fake trading app takes *₹2.3 crore* from RC Puram retiree
tldr: A 76-year-old retired PSU executive transferred over ₹2.4 crore in 19 transactions between Aug 21 and Nov 13 to third-party accounts after a caller pitched forex and commodity trades. When he tried to withdraw, he was asked for fees and the withdrawal option was disabled.

beats.what: Cyberabad cybercrime police booked a case over a fake online trading platform fraud.
beats.why: Scammers pose as trading desks and use third-party bank and UPI accounts.
beats.care: Victims can call the 1930 cybercrime helpline; fees to withdraw are a warning sign.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 20): the complaint was filed on Nov 18 and the case registered under BNS and IT Act sections.

cards.q: Would you spot a fake trading app before investing?

qs: Why do small 'returns' make people trust a fake platform?
Should banks flag repeated transfers to third-party accounts?

facts.t: He transferred over ₹2.4 crore in *19 transactions* to accounts in third parties' names.

viz.verdict: Fraud ran for nearly three months

watch: Cyberabad cybercrime police are investigating the accounts used in the transfers.
